lessons.title: An chéad díochlaonadh: an ginideach uatha
lessons.en: First declension: genitive singular with an
lessons.rule: When a noun follows another noun such as barr, doras or lár, it goes into the genitive: after an, put séimhiú on it and make its last consonant slender, so an crann becomes barr an chrainn.
steps: Put séimhiú on the first letter: crann becomes chrann.
Make the last consonant slender by putting i after the last vowel: chrainn.
Write it after an: Thit an cat ó bharr an chrainn.

example.prompt: Thit an cat ó bharr an (crann).
example.answer: Thit an cat ó bharr an chrainn.

more.answer: Chuaigh muid go deireadh an bhóthair.

lessons.hint: After an: séimhiú at the start, i before the last consonant.

lessons.title: An chéad díochlaonadh: s, d, t agus guta
lessons.en: First declension: nouns beginning with s, d, t or a vowel
lessons.rule: Make the end slender as usual, but watch the first letter: after an, s followed by a vowel becomes ts (an tsagairt), while d, t, sc and vowels do not change (an tuaiscirt, an scéil, an asail).
steps: Make the last consonant slender: sagart becomes sagairt.
It begins with s and a vowel, so put t in front of it after an: an tsagairt.
Write the sentence: Ar chuala tú guth an tsagairt ag an Aifreann?

example.prompt: Ar chuala tú guth an (sagart) ag an Aifreann?
example.answer: Ar chuala tú guth an tsagairt ag an Aifreann?

more.answer: Bhí gasúr ar dhroim an asail.

lessons.hint: s + vowel becomes ts; d, t and vowels stay as they are.

lessons.title: An chéad díochlaonadh: an ginideach gan alt
lessons.en: First declension: genitive without the article
lessons.rule: With no an in front, do not add séimhiú: just make the last consonant slender, so arán becomes píosa aráin. A boy's or man's name is the exception: it takes séimhiú too (Cathal, camán Chathail).
steps: There is no an before the noun, so do not add séimhiú.
Make the last consonant slender: arán becomes aráin.
Write the sentence: Bhí píosa aráin ar an phláta.

example.answer: Bhí píosa aráin ar an phláta.

lessons.hint: No an: only make the end slender; names also take séimhiú.

lessons.title: An chéad díochlaonadh: an ginideach iolra
lessons.rule: In the genitive plural keep na, go back to the singular form of the noun and eclipse it: na cupáin becomes meáchan na gcupán. Before a vowel, drop the h and put n- instead (na héin, nead na n-éan).
steps: Go back to the singular form of the noun: na bochtáin, bochtán.
Eclipse it after na: b becomes mb, na mbochtán.
Write the sentence: Bailíonn an scoil airgead ar son na mbochtán.

example.prompt: Bailíonn an scoil airgead ar son (na bochtáin).
example.answer: Bailíonn an scoil airgead ar son na mbochtán.

more.answer: Tá muintir na n-oileán ag fanacht leis an bhád.

lessons.title: An dara díochlaonadh: an t-iolra
lessons.rule: Most second-declension nouns make the plural by adding -í (pingin, pinginí), -eanna or -anna (sráid, sráideanna; fadhb, fadhbanna) or -a (duilleog, duilleoga); learn the plural along with the word.
steps: Find the noun: pingin, which takes -í in the plural.
Add the ending: pinginí.
Write it after na: Chuir sé na pinginí sa sparán.

example.answer: Chuir sé na pinginí sa sparán.

lessons.title: An dara díochlaonadh: an ginideach uatha
lessons.rule: After na in the genitive singular, a feminine noun takes no séimhiú (h before a vowel): add -e to the end, making the last consonant slender first if it is broad (sráid, barr na sráide; bialann, lár na bialainne).
steps: The last consonant of bialann is broad, so make it slender: bialainn.
Add -e: bialainne.
Write it after na with no séimhiú: Bhí muid inár suí i lár na bialainne in Iúr Cinn Trá.

lessons.title: An dara díochlaonadh: an ginideach iolra
lessons.rule: In the genitive plural keep na and eclipse the noun. If the plural was made by adding -a, take the -a off again (na fuinneoga, gloine na bhfuinneog); any other plural ending stays (na tíortha, bratacha na dtíortha).
steps: The plural fuinneoga was made by adding -a, so take it off: fuinneog.
Eclipse it after na: f becomes bhf, na bhfuinneog.
Write the phrase: Gloine na bhfuinneog.
lessons.hint: Urú after na; drop a plural -a.

lessons.title: An ginideach i ndiaidh an ainm bhriathartha
lessons.rule: A noun that comes after a verbal noun such as ag glanadh or ag léamh goes into the genitive, just as it would after another noun: ag glanadh an chlóis, ag léamh na ceiste, ag léamh na gceisteanna.
steps: The noun follows ag glanadh, so it goes into the genitive.
Clós is masculine: put séimhiú on it after an and make the end slender, an chlóis.
Write the phrase: ag glanadh an chlóis.
lessons.hint: After ag + verbal noun, use the genitive.

tables.title: An Dara Díochlaonadh: Iolraí (cumtar an uimhir iolra)
forms: (i) Trí -í a chur leis an fhocal: Oifig, Oifigí
(ii) Trí -anna, -eanna a chur leis an fhocal: Scoil, Scoileanna; Ceist, Ceisteanna
(iii) Trí -a a chur leis an fhocal: Amharclann, Amharclanna
(iv) Trí -acha a chur leis an fhocal: Craobh, Craobhacha

tables.title: An Dara Díochlaonadh: samplaí, uatha agus iolra, ainmneach agus ginideach
forms: 1 (-e): An scoil, na scoileanna; Doras na scoile, Doirse na scoileanna
2 (each > í): An ghirseach, na girseacha; Cóta na girsí, cótaí na ngirseach
3 (caolú + e): An phictiúrlann, na pictiúrlanna; Clár na pictiúrlainne, cláracha na bpictiúrlann
4 (-e) Focail a thosaíonn ar ghuta: An oifig, na hoifigí; Doras na hoifige, doirse na n-oifigí

tables.title: Déantar caolú de réir na rialacha seo
forms: ea > ei: speach, speiche. Ach: cearc, circe
